utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We are going into closed session as the witness enters court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your evidence will continue this morning. It's important that you remember that the declaration you made at the very beginning of your evidence to tell the truth continues to apply to that evidence -- the evidence that you give today. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good morning, K83. We left off yesterday talking about the Cegar units and Cegar 1. I want you -- I asked you about the uniform of the Cegar unit yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What -- you said the units had a camouflage uniform and then they had a vest on top of that one that said "police" on the back. Do you remember the colour of the uniform, the camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The colour was green, military camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the vest was the same colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except for the white letters that said "policija," "police."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were the Cegar units stationed in Suva Reka or outside Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part was in Suva Reka and another part was in the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know where they had their base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Forgive me one moment, Your Honour. I have to stand and turn off and on the microphone. It's a little inconvenient with the set-up I've made. One moment. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know -- the police units, would you describe them as ordinary police units or special police units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regular police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. I now return to the events as they unfolded on the 26th of March. You explained yesterday you returned from patrol and then you saw Cegar 1 and his units in front of the police station. I'd now like to show you a picture of that area and ask if you can help us explain where you saw these different units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we see P2349, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, while we wait for the picture to come up -- oh, there it was. You said there were two trucks yesterday. Did Cegar 1 come with a third vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he gave came with his Land Rover.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If the usher would assist the witness with a pen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, I will ask if you on this picture could indicate approximately where you saw the two trucks that the Cegar units had come in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here two trucks, and Cegar 1 with his vehicle was parked here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Would you please put the letter A where you saw -- where the trucks were and the letter B where Cegar 1's car was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Would you put the letter B where Cegar 1's Land Rover was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the police station, could you put the letter C on the police station or the SUP, if you see it on this picture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And where were you when you came back from the patrol? Where did you stop your car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in front of the SUP building on the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Then what happened? Could you explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were watching them getting off the truck, that is to say the police, and we saw them move towards the road to Restane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did Cegar 1 speak to anyone from the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we watched them getting out and go into the first houses opposite the SUP, he walked up to the assistant commander, Nenad Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did Cegar 1 say anything to Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that we shouldn't be watching but that we should follow right behind him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In what voice did he say that? Was he just speaking normally? Was he giving orders? Was he yelling? How would you describe the way he was speaking to Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the assistant commander saluted back properly. Cegar 1 didn't even want to greet him properly. He was just shouting. He said: "Get going." So he was furious.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know why he was furious?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Maybe because we were watching, maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Can he mark the place where they were standing, please, where they were available because then this will make the picture complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, where on this picture were Cegar 1 and Jovanovic standing when this took place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in front of the SUP building, that is to say somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The witness had made a red dot just above the red car that can be seen in front of the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, how did Jovanovic react when he had been yelled at by Cegar 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Nenad Jovanovic, assistant commander, just said that we should get going in a sort of lost way. We didn't know where, what for, why. We didn't know what to do. But we just blindly set off towards the first houses that were there, and Cegar's men were walking ahead of us and we were following them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you walking or running, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was sort of running -- well, fast running at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we got to the house where the OSCE had been previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who were with you at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, assistant commander Nenad Jovanovic; Radovan Tanovic; Cukaric, Sladjan; and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you to take up a position somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since Sladjan Cukaric was head of the patrol, he ordered us to stop on the left and right side of the house so that no one would shoot at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you see the house on this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you -- would you mark with the letter D, like delta, where you took up position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who was on the -- you said, "we took up position." Who was the other person who took up position with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miki Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where was he positioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was on the other side, on the back side of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. When -- on this picture it looks like there is -- there are some bushes or something next to and in front of the house close to where you were standing. At the time was that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And there's also -- there's some sort of a fence in front of the white vehicles that can be seen in the back of the OSCE house. At the time was that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a wall there about 2 metres or even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you make a line where the wall you're talking about was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. From -- from where you were standing, did you have a clear view down along the house and down to the back of the OSCE house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We can see it on the picture, but approximately how far would you estimate it was from where you were standing and down to the back of the OSCE house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was about 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you describe what you -- what you saw from where you were positioned when you had -- when you had been taking up positions, you were watching down, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shooting was coming from all sides, so I was afraid and I went towards the house by the road, you see, where the OSCE had been.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You say you were afraid. What were you afraid of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because there was gun-fire coming from all sides. You didn't know where they were shooting there from. There was no shelter for me to hide.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cegar's units were shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: While you were still at the position you have marked with D, did anybody come out from the house where you were close to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I heard your answer but I think it didn't get translated. Could you answer again, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that house, women and children came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How did they come out? Were they running? Were they walking? What was the situation like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They started running. They were frightened, and they started fleeing towards the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When they had run out of the house, did you move from your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where did you first go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got to Tanovic and Cukaric because they were looking at the IDs of four persons who were by the house -- or rather, behind the OSCE house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you indicate with the letter E like echo approximately where Cegar and his -- and the other persons were, the four detained men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you were somewhere behind that, is that what you are saying, but relatively close by. Is that how I understand it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was somewhere around the middle, that would mean around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The witness has made a dot a little under the E that he just placed on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you describe what you saw then. Did Cegar do anything to the men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you answer that, I think we are talking about someone called Tanovic and someone called Cukaric. Now, does Cegar come in somewhere as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No, that's my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tanovic and Cukaric first looked at the IDs of these persons. They took their documents and they were facing the wall, their faces were turned to the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then they said to me that I should escort -- or rather, follow these persons who left the house, women, children, old men, to see where they were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to the four men that were lined up against the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were killed right by the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you saw that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were shooting at them already as I was passing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You were told that you should follow the people that had ran out. And what were you to do once you had followed them, should you just follow them or should you do something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just supposed to see where they were going and to inform Cukaric and Tanovic as to where they went further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could I ask you to draw a line on the map from the point you made below the E and then tracking the approximate route that you went.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you pass over the bus station from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was this passageway here and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you -- I know you might be making a line through the houses because the passageway is too narrow to be seen on the photograph, but could you make a line to the approximate place where you went on the -- on the bus station.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then from the place where you have made the line now, where did you go? Oh, sorry, excuse me, before I ask you to continue the line, did you see any -- any people on the -- at the bus station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw two elderly men -- or rather, a man and an elderly woman who were lying on the sidewalk. They had been wounded in the legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could I ask you to make the letter F at the approximate place where the -- the two elderly persons were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Before this gets too complicated, I think we should maybe make this an exhibit and then continue with a clean copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That will be necessary, will it? Will we run into difficulty if we don't continue to see this -- presumably we're heading for the cafe or the pizza, are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Let's make sure we have saved a copy of this and we can continue to work on it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC47, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, from where the F is, where did you go? What route did you take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We set out to the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you draw on this picture the route that you took to the pizzeria, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, what you need to do is bring up IC47 and then start drawing on top of it I think. We've lost what we had so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think we still have the old ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, K83, we're just trying to re-call the drawing you just did and nothing to do with you. That's me who's giving confusing directions. Right. K83, we have the picture back again. So you've marked with an F the location -- the approximate location where the two elderly persons were lying on the ground, shot in the leg. You then went to the place you call the pizzeria. Could you show us what route you took to get to that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you stop at the point that you have reached now or did you go -- or did you go further down in the direction of the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I could see, that these civilians, the elderly people and the children, were in the pizzeria, and then I returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could I ask that you put the letter G at the approximate place where the pizzeria is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You said you could see the civilians. Were they inside or outside the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were inside the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were there any other people in uniform around that area when you walked down towards the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were none.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is it possible for you to estimate how many people were in or around the pizzeria at the time you looked down in that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but approximately 35 to 40 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned to Cukaric and Tanovic to tell them that the people were in the pizzeria and that they were locked up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by locked up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had the key, so they locked themselves up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How do you know they had locked themselves up in the pizzeria? Were you down there to -- to see it or is it something you were told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The door was locked; it couldn't be opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- did you meet Cukaric and Tanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where did you approximately see them? You don't need to mark it on the map, if you can just describe where you saw them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we met on the road where the vehicles are parked in front of the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What -- how were you feeling at that point in time? Were you still frightened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was very scared and under stress, since it all happened quickly, including the shooting. And they told me to go to the closest restaurant or bar to get a drink to try and calm down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where -- where is the restaurant or kiosk or shop you went into? If you make a dot first so we can see that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The witness has made a dot just above the F that he made a little earlier to indicate the place he went into to have something to drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you then pick up something to drink and came out again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took two bottles of liquor. There was a cognac or brandy or vodka. I can't recall. When I was returning, the people who were on the sidewalk who had been alive previously when I passed by, they were now dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That is the two elderly people. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How do you know they were dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I passed by on my way to fetch a drink, they were still alive, but as I was coming back, they were dead, they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: From what you could see, do you think they had died from the wounds they had received earlier or do you think something happened to them between the two times you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were shot in the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: After you have seen that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, I think at this stage we should make what we have now an exhibit and change to another view of the same scenario as we proceed. So let's first make this an in-court exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be IC48, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then I'd like to see the second page of this same exhibit we have on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, while we're sorting out the technological stuff here, when you had come out and you were taking the two bottles and you saw the two elderly people that had been shot and were lying on the ground, did you -- where did you go? You can just tell me first if you can just describe where you went to and we'll make a mark afterwards on the picture we have on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went to the area between the pizzeria and this building, this is where we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before we move on to this, Mr. Marcussen, is there no help that you can obtain for us on who was responsible for the deaths of the elderly couple? Is there just nothing on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Let's have a try.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know -- you saw that the two elderly people had been shot in the head. Do you know who shot them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sladjan Cukaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see him do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him, he had a rifle in his hand when I came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see him fire the rifle or was he just close by the bodies with a rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was close to the body and he had a rifle, and I also heard a shot. This was all very close by; we are talking about 5 or 6 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- at that point in time was he facing in the direction of the bodies or was he walking away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was leaving from where the bodies were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. So you -- you went back to the narrow alley-way and you made a dot on the map here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you -- could you see down into the direction of the pizzeria at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment we couldn't see because this is a narrow passageway. The pizzeria is from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: At --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The witness has just made a line to indicate where the pizzeria is around the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So where you were now at this point in time, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we drank up the two bottles of liquor so that I would calm down, and my colleagues drank as well. We drank up quickly, and then Cukaric smashed a shop window belonging to the pizzeria using his rifle-butt and he threw in a hand-grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Let me just break this series of events up in some smaller pieces with you. Who were you -- you was together with a number of people you said and you were drinking the liquor. Who were you with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sladjan Cukaric, Radovan Tanovic, Miki Petkovic, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you all had something to drink from the bottles. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And was it -- were you drinking from the two bottles you had collected or had other people collected bottles as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we drank from the bottle I had brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You then described that you saw Cukaric smash the window to the pizzeria. When you saw that, when were you standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was still here at the corner that I just marked. We were standing there all the while.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. So later when we look at this picture we need to be able to recognise this. Could I ask you to mark an A at the approximate location of the corner where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: From the corner where you were standing, could you see down in the direction of the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment I couldn't because I tried to take cover because of the hand-grenade that he was about to throw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see the window being smashed by -- did you see the window break and being smashed, did you see the person making that movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that moment. I only heard the glass being broken, and later on I heard the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who do you say threw in the grenade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hand-grenade was -- the first hand-grenade was thrown by Sladjan Cukaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How do you know that? Did you see it, see him throw in the hand-grenade or prepare to throw in the hand-grenade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first he took out a hand-grenade and started moving towards the shop window, getting ready to throw it. And he told us to take cover so that we wouldn't be hurt by any of the shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: After the hand-grenade had exploded, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We waited for two or three minutes for everything to calm down, and then a second hand-grenade was thrown.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know who threw the second hand-grenade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second hand-grenade was thrown by Radovan Tanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was getting ready for another attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Between the two hand-grenades, was there any shooting coming down from the direction of the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were waiting for everything to settle after the first grenade, to have the smoke cleared, after that Tanovic and Cukaric took turns. They used bursts of fire from their automatic rifles, shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then the second grenade was thrown in, and was there then shooting after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was firing from automatic rifles. I said that. They used bursts of fire, and one could still hear screams and moaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you participate in the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you asked to participate in the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked if I wanted to participate, but since they realised I was in no condition to do that, they didn't force me to. I was kind of lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who -- who were "they"? You referred to somebody.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cukaric and Tanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- you described being up in the area of the corner that you have marked with an A and then there were the hand-grenade and the shooting and the hand-grenade and the shooting. After that, did you -- did it become quiet in the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you move from the corner where you had been standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I moved. I passed by the pizzeria. I went as far as the kiosk here, next to the road, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed there throughout until the team arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did we get a mark for where the corner of the -- where the kiosk was?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, we only have a dot. I was going to get to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where is the dot?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Would you mark a B, please, at the place where you took up position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you instructed to take up that position or did you just go there on your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was told to stay there and see -- or rather, to prevent people coming close to the pizzeria so that they wouldn't see what was happening. As for Miki Petkovic, he stayed up where we were -- where we had been previously, next to the letter A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who told you to take up the position at the point B you have marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sladjan Cukaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I need to go back a little bit in time. Before the first grenade was thrown in and you were up in the -- in the area of where you put the A, were there anybody communicating on the radio at that point in time among the people you were with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't hear anything precisely. All I know is Cukaric had two Motorolas. As for who he communicated with, I really couldn't hear, I can't say. I don't know whether he talked to anyone or whether he received any orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But you did see him use his radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did he use -- if you know, did he use one or both of the radios? I think you said he had two.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had two, but I don't know which one he used exactly. I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were -- I'm going back -- sorry, I forgot to ask you this when we were at the right place in the chronology. Now I'd like to take you back to the point when you were at point B. When you took up position at point B, what did you see -- could you describe what you were seeing when you were up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A truck arrived from the direction of Prizren. But before the truck, Dr. Boban was already there, together with Djordjevic. I can't remember his first name. So before the truck, Dr. Boban and the staff commander Djordjevic had arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know the family name of Dr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vuksanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And do you -- what -- what -- what position did he hold, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he commanded the civil protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And Djordjevic, what position did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djordjevic was commander of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is that the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How -- approximately how long after you had come down to point B did it take before Vuksanovic and Djordjevic came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then you explained a truck came. How long after Vuksanovic and Djordjevic did it take before the truck arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truck arrived some half an hour later, from the direction of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: On this photograph, is the direction of Prizren, is that left or right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know what organisation or unit the truck belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truck was some civilian truck. I don't know what organisation. It didn't have any special markings or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were there any -- apart from the driver, were there anybody in the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know who they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. That was the first time I saw these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know what function they -- they had when they were not -- before this day, do you know what these people were doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did they work for anybody, for the Territorial Defence, for the civilian -- for civilian protection, something like that, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people who came on that day, I don't know whether they worked for some organisation. That was the first time I saw these people in that truck, over there, in Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What happened when the truck arrived? Where did it park?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It parked here, this entrance here that I marked with a B a few minutes ago. So it backed off here and then it practically got to the pizzeria itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then a team came from the civilian protection to load the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How do you know the team that came were from the civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had the clothes that civilian protection people wear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when the civilian protection people came, what did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at first they didn't know. Dr. Boban Vuksanovic got these people from their lunch. It was lunchtime, and these people previously were herding cattle and they were trying to get this cattle on to a truck, but these people didn't know what they were supposed to do on that day at all, that day when Dr. Boban Vuksanovic called them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Having arrived at the pizzeria, what did they -- what did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they all started running away. No one wanted to do this, you know, when they saw the blood -- well, first of all, these were people, say, 50 years old, 60 years old, to the age of 15, actually. They were children. They felt nauseous. They couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did they -- were they forced to do it nonetheless, take the bodies out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Afterwards Cukaric took over the command and said: Who doesn't want to load these bodies is going to end up the same way as those corpses, the people who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so the young and the elderly men who had come that you described from the civil protection, they loaded the bodies on to the truck. And could you see when they were loading the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Once I sort of cast a glance, sort of. It was an ugly scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When the truck was full, I take it that it left. What direction did it go in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it went back to Prizren. It went in the direction of Prizren. It came from Prizren and went back to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did another truck come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, immediately after that one another truck came.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did they continue to load bodies on that truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman called Jashar Berisha?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jashar Berisha worked for many years at the gasoline station in Suva Reka. I know him. I know him as a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see him around this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on that day -- well, he worked at the gasoline station, but when this gun-fire started he was detained up there at the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see him being detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him being detained, but I know that he worked and that he was there until the gun-fire started. Once the gun-fire started, he was no longer there. I thought that he went home; however, he was up there at the SUP, at the police station. And he was brought in from the police station. He was brought in, in a vehicle, to the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Can you see the petrol station on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you go over to the petrol station close to where the pumps are, and I think there's an office or something behind -- previous to this day, had you been over there after the shooting had started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When you saw Jashar Berisha, you say he came from the direction of the police station. How did he arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was brought in by the patrol to the pizzeria, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you know any of the officers who brought him in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I just remember Todor Jovanovic from then. I cannot remember all those names now, of all the people who were in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So am I correct, you -- you infer from the fact that -- that Jashar Berisha came in a car from the police station that he must have been detained when -- when the shooting started, but you didn't actually see him being detained. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had indicated that we were going to spend an hour and a half with this witness. I have already hit an hour and 35 minutes. I only have another five minutes. I hope that will be permissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, after Jashar Berisha had arrived, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jashar Berisha got out of the official vehicle and he had already seen that truck, where the corpses were being loaded. And he was struggling. He didn't want to go towards the truck. And he just said that he didn't deserve that, to go there to the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- so you were watching as he was going down in the direction of the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I was right there by the road, by the kiosk. That's where the vehicle had stopped, and he got out of that vehicle and they were dragging him there to the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so you remember him saying that he didn't deserve that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was speaking to Dr. Boban Vuksanovic personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he was struggling to break free, in a way he was trying to run away, to get out of that, but Cukaric just grabbed his arm, pushed him away, and fired a burst of gun-fire from his automatic rifle into the man's back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you saw Cukaric shoot at Jashar Berisha?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not the only one who saw it. People from the municipality saw it, too, who were in the municipality and people from the Territorial Defence. Many people saw that scene and saw what he did on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know what they did to his body after he had been shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was also loaded on to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When all the -- this was over and the second truck left, what direction did it take off in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Likewise, the direction of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: After it was all over, did you go to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed with those people from the civilian protection because Cukaric was forcing them to put sand and soil into the pizzeria so that the blood stains would not remain there; however, there wasn't any sand and they couldn't -- couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When -- when that couldn't be cleaned up with sand and earth, did Cukaric doing anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cukaric went -- well, now I can't remember, was it with the commanders or these other people. He left. Tanovic stayed there and just set fire to this curtain that was next to the shop window. And there was nothing else inside that could burn; everything was made of metal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like that if we could make what we have on the screen now an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC49, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then could we see Exhibit P117, page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, is this the place you referred to as the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. After the civil protection people had tried to clean up and the curtains had been burned, did you return to your home that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did -- on a later occasion, did you go -- another day did you go back to the house of the Berishas, together with a team of investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the next day -- well, regular activities. I mean, well the next day at work -- well, that's to say we started working and we had to show the civil defence team where these bodies were, and those bodies were supposed to be collected because it was summertime and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who directed you to go and show where the bodies were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, which bodies are we talking about now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, apart from the civil defence people, were there any -- were there any investigators -- was an investigation carried out before the bodies were moved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were people who were crime scene technicians taking pictures of that, photographing that. Do you understand what I'm saying? They were loaded on to a truck and they were buried under some kind of codes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of any of the crime scene technicians and where they came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember because Todor Jovanovic worked there in Suva Reka and some came from Prizren. I remember some Mojsic, but I don't know his first name exactly and this other colleague of his. I don't know, I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where did you -- what location did you first go to when the bodies were to be collected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first we went to the house where the Berishas were -- rather, we called it the OSCE house. First them, there were four men there. The next day there was the corpse of a woman there, too, a woman of 50 or 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- did you see the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the bodies. The woman, her leg and part of her arm had been burned. I don't know how. I didn't see the woman that day, but I don't know how she came to be there on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: After -- after you had been at the OSCE house, did you continue to other locations in Suva Reka with the same team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. We went on to -- well, to the SUP and then towards Restane to see whether there were some other corpses left in some houses. We found other corpses along the way in other houses. For the most part they were men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If you know, do you know how they died? I mean, have they been killed by gun-fire? How did they die, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had been killed. Now, how, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You said you went up along the Restane road. Is that -- you basically followed the same road that the Cegar units had been taking. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Because they had passed there and we wanted to check whether there were any corpses left there, because it was summertime and we didn't want a disease to spread or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, I may have missed that. Was there evidence that they went along the Restane road?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I believe that yesterday the witness testified that they were following up that way, but otherwise we can just clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, if you could think back at the day when you were at the Berisha house, again when you had been at the house of the Berishas or the OSCE house, there were the Cegar units and there were people from the SUP. The operation that the Cegar unit was involved in, in what direction did that operation go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as for the surrounding houses, that is to say these houses along the Restane road, I mean well they took that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- did you see them move out in that direction; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're talking about the same day, are we? Because we had evidence yesterday about battles going on, on the road to Restane, about 3 to 5 kilometres from Suva Reka and so forth, terrorist attacks; we had that sort of evidence. But did we have evidence that this unit had gone along that road?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You're -- I could be mistaken. As I refresh my memory the evidence we got yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Every killing that we have so far heard of from this witness, as far as I have recorded it - and of course that may be incomplete - every one seems to be said the responsibility of Cukaric and the other colleagues or colleague mainly who was with him. I don't know that I have -- I have a record of the Cegar group shooting at random at the outset of this incident, but no indication from this witness of any deaths resulting from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think that's going -- the witness's evidence is that the Cegar units when the up along the Restane road. The witness don't know, as I am aware at least, that the Cegar units killed anyone. The witness's evidence also is that the following day they, people from the SUP and crime scene investigators, went up the Restane road and they found more bodies. We would make submissions on that later, but I think that is what the evidence is so far. I can try to clarify this with the witness if it would assist, but we are not trying to state the evidence any higher than what I've just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'm simply saying to you that I don't have a note of the evidence that you seem to be relying on that -- to the effect that they went along that road. And it may be I haven't noted it, but I don't recollect it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, on the day that the incident took place at the OSCE house, to your knowledge did the Cegar unit continue up along the road towards Restane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They continued up along the rode road towards Restane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, that concludes our questions at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll have a break now. You should stay where you are while the court rises, and then someone will make arrangements to show you where to wait during our break. We'll break now for 30 minutes and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Private session again while the witness enters court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, meanwhile you could perhaps tell me the running order.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. General Pavkovic, General Lukic, General Ojdanic, Mr. Sainovic, Mr. Milutinovic, and General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Open session].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: K83, you will now be examined by various counsel for the accused, and the first of these will be for Mr. Pavkovic, and that will be Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I have just a couple of questions. It will be very brief. During these events you have just described that took place in Suva Reka, it's the case, isn't it, that there was no army presence in Suva Reka at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: With regard to these two people you talked about who arrived on the scene after these killings, Djordjevic and Dr. Boban Vuksanovic, do you know what happened to them after that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You don't know that they were both killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have some indication that they were killed by the KLA. Can you confirm that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I represent Mr. Sreten Lukic, along with my colleagues, Branko Lukic and Ozren Ogrizovic relative to these proceedings. Today I'm going to have to ask you some questions relative to your testimony that you've just given to try and clarify and better understand things. I would ask you to pay close attention to what I am asking and try to give me the most accurate and concise answer possible since our time here is limited and we have a number of things to deal with. And due to the protective measures given to you I must call you K83, so please remember if I do use that terminology I am referring to you and I will proceed. Now, first of all I would like to ask you a few questions to clear up the structure and operation of the police station, that is to say the OUP in Suva Reka, O-U-P. Now, first of all isn't it correct that the public security division, the RJB, and the state security division, the RDB, were separate structures with a separate hierarchy, separate computer databases, and separate information channels within the OUP in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as far as the state security or RDB presence in Suva Reka, is it accurate to state that it was small and consisted of approximately two persons or so during the time period of 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how big was the rest of the OUP in Suva Reka, that is to say in terms of the regular and reserve policemen? How many of their -- them were you assigned to the OUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is it accurate to state that a clear majority of the persons in the -- operating in the OUP of Suva Reka were locals from the Suva Reka municipality itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And is it correct to state that the OUP of Suva Reka actually fell under the jurisdiction of the SUP, S-U-P, or [B/C/S spoken] of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And is it also accurate to state that in the course of regular duties the OUP of Suva Reka would have to report to the SUP in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And as far as you know, the OUP of Suva Reka would only report to the SUP in Prizren and not to any other structures within the MUP. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned some crime scene investigators, an investigative team that came out to Suva Reka and to the Berisha house with you the day after the killings that you testified to. Was this investigative team from the Prizren SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can concentrate on the time-period that these -- that this investigative team was there, is it accurate to state that you did not take this investigative team to the pizzeria location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The investigative team that came the day after the killings, it was not taken to the pizzeria location, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And on the occasion when this investigative team was at the Berisha house where there was now the body also of a female, is it accurate that upon that day the investigative team was shot upon by weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the Berisha house. It was a bit further down towards Restane where the bodies were buried at the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that someone shot upon -- shot at the investigative team --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the investigative team, was it -- it was accompanied by regularly marked MUP vehicles. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you and the other MUP officials were wearing uniforms at the time that were MUP uniforms. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So that whoever shot at you was targeting persons that were clearly identified as being the police. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you just mentioned the cemetery. Is it also accurate that after the investigation the bodies that were found were buried in single -- in individual graves, each grave marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Each body was marked with a code and they were buried individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And based upon your experience in the police force, was this standard operating procedure for crime scene investigation and for burial of bodies that were discovered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And had that been the standard operating procedure, even in the years long before 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the -- sometime in 2003, you were called in by the police authorities to be interviewed relative to an investigation relating to the events in Suva Reka. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at that point in time, you gave your first statement to the police authorities of the Republic of Serbia, detailing your account of what had happened and who was responsible for it. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that was part of an ongoing investigation at that point in time. Subsequently, the judicial authorities undertook a judicial prosecution of your colleagues who were involved in the event at Suva Reka on March the 25th, 1999. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to return back to finish up a few more specific questions about the operation of the Suva Reka police station or the OUP. First of all, we -- we would like to ask you about a man by the name of Miskovic, who also was known as Nisevic with the first name Misko. Now, was he -- strike that. He was not the overall commander or head of all the MUP police in Suva Reka, was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't the overall commander. He was not a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clearing that up for me. In fact, this Miskovic or Nisevic, in fact he was merely one of the two or three DB policemen, that is to say the state security personnel in Suva Reka. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact, do you even know if this Miskovic or Nisevic, however you want to refer to him, whether he held any rank in the structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He always wore civilian clothes, hence I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now this individual, this Miskovic or Nisevic, he was a local from the town of Suva Reka. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I believe you testified that he owned a hotel called the Hotel Boss. Was this hotel located in Shiroko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you have any knowledge of an attack that occurred on September the 12th, 1998, in this village of Shiroko during which terrorists attacked the Hotel Boss that was owned by Mr. Miskovic or Mr. Nisevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see to what extent it was damaged, but I did hear that a projectile was launched at the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And -- and do you recall another event that occurred in 1998 in front of a trafika or a little shop in which someone shot at Miskovic, Nisevic, and in fact, I think, wounded him and killed one other person. Do you recall that event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so. Misko stopped by the kiosk that day to by a newspaper. From some 20 metres away, fire was opened with the intent of killing him, but instead they killed the Albanian who was selling the newspapers, whereas Misko was only wounded in his hand. It was not a serious injury.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe you had -- had mentioned that this gentleman usually wore civilian clothes. Do you know whether in fact he was wearing civilian clothes on the day that this attack occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. He always wore civilian clothes. Neither before the war or during the war, he did not have a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was this gentleman Nisevic, Miskovic, was he well-known in the Suva Reka town by the general populace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone knew him, the Serbs, the Albanians, because he had a driving school there and also the check-up of vehicles, that was his business. He also had a hotel and a number of shops and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, we may return to some more questions about this individual later. I'd like to focus now on some background information relative to your experiences. Is it correct that you became a police reservist in approximately 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And from 1994 to 1997, apart from your training as a reserve police officer, did you have occasion to perform police duties in Suva Reka municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And on the occasions - again, focussing on the years 1994 through 1997 - that you did perform police duties, is it a fact that you would have a daily report with a Lieutenant Repanovic, who would give a briefing to you and to the other police officers going on patrol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me personally, since I was a reservist policeman, but heads of patrols and professional policemen had to compile reports, also fill out patrol forms. They had to type them out, and they needed to type out reports as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that question may have been misunderstood because of the use of the words "daily report."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think so as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think you meant a briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever participate in any briefing before going out on patrol, and again during the years 1994 through 1997 first of all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean by briefings?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prior to going out on a patrol, would someone from the police station give you your daily assignments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was done by the leader of the shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And during 1998 and 1999, did this same procedure remain in place, this giving of daily assignments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, on the critical date in question, March 25th, 1999, when you and your colleagues went to the Berisha house and the pizzeria, that day you had not been given a daily assignment at the SUP to -- to undertake what happened that day, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's -- let's go back to the time period before 1998 very briefly. You had mentioned some check-points that were in existence in -- along the road outside Suva Reka. Is it true that these check-points existed even in the year 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was the primary purpose of these check-points to control traffic and dissuade the armed terrorist elements from disrupting traffic on the roadway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, prior to the year 1998, how was the situation in the Suva Reka municipality? And that is to say was there a problem caused by the presence of armed Albanian fighters, whether they went by any name or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they -- at that time the OSCE was there and they monitored all police movement. There was always a vehicle in front and another one at the back, but when the attack took place both vehicles would drive off and we would remain behind at their mercy. And once the firing stopped, then they would come back and they would try and establish who opened fire, who was wounded, and to see what took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to have to try and clarify that with you. I had asked you about the time-period prior to 1998, but let's talk about what you describe. You described the OSCE. The OSCE was there at the end of 1998 and for the first few months of 1999. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in -- in the answer you gave to the prior question you said: "There was always a vehicle in front and another one at the back." Is it accurate to state that those vehicles in the front and in the back would be the OSCE vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then I take it the vehicles in the middle would be the regular MUP patrol vehicles. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say that the vehicles would drive off and we would remain behind at their mercy, who is the "they" at whose mercy the police would be left at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now -- now that we've cleared that up, I'd like to now move to the original issue that I'd wanted to ask you about. Is it correct that in 1998 things started changing for the worse in Suva Reka town and municipality, and that is to say that from 1998 onwards the terrorists began operating in Suva Reka municipality. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in particular, among the things that started getting worse in 1998, is it accurate that persons started being kidnapped by these terrorists from public buses in Suva Reka municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it accurate to state that from 1998 onwards, you were essentially a full-time police officer within the OUP of Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now during that time-period, that is to say 1998 onwards, did you have any knowledge or information that the persons being kidnapped by these terrorists were in fact both ethnic Albanians and ethnic Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first there were Albanians who were loyal citizens. They were not kidnapped only but also killed, and the next day a corpse was found by the road. As for the Serbs that had been kidnapped, they went missing and none of them was ever found.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know approximately how many such incidents of either kidnappings or killings of Suva Reka citizens by the terrorists occurred in either 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Suva Reka there were four cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say "in Suva Reka," that would be in the town itself. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the town itself, the surrounding area, 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And were there also -- you mentioned at least one instance of an attack upon a police vehicle. Were there also multiple instances of attacks by these terrorists in the Suva Reka region upon regular police patrols or police buildings or police personnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Practical every time there was any kind of movement, any kind of departure from the SUP building, they regularly monitored this. And whenever the patrol would leave the SUP, it would be attacked. For the most part, people would get wounded, but there were even fatalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And these fatalities and woundings, were these what you had referenced earlier as to reasons why the police force did not have sufficient personnel as of 1998? Was that one of the reasons people were even leaving or the police force did not have enough personnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were afraid. They didn't want to get killed, and they would leave the service and go to their homes in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know of an instance -- strike that. Do you know of a killing of an Albanian policeman from the Suva Reka state security organ at the hands of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was Iljaz, I don't know his last name, Iljaz, Iljaz, he worked in the DB. He was killed in his very own home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you know at the time where the KLA terrorists were situated, that is to say from what areas or villages they were based in the Suva Reka municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part towards Budakovo, Gornji Kruscica, Malisevo. I don't know. There's quite a few of these places of theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say there's quite a few of these places of theirs, would it be accurate to state that the terrorists held these regions so that regular police patrols dared not even enter that territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the municipality of Suva Reka there was 5 per cent of Serbs, that is to say that 95 per cent were Albanians. So Serbs could not cover all these territories. They didn't have enough personnel for all of that, to keep it blocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And was there even some reported terrorist activity within the town of Suva Reka itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand. Could you repeat the question, if you can?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. Let me perhaps rephrase it. Were there even areas of Suva Reka town itself that were not safe for police patrols to go through because of the threat posed by terrorists in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was danger. There were cases when a Serb would get killed, a Serb who worked in a shop, in broad daylight at 10.00, at the work-place, in the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me ask you if you recall an instance with a -- with a number of such fatalities that occurred on or about January 8th, 1999, when there was an attack by the terrorists from the direction of Dulje upon a patrol on the road that left three policemen dead, four policemen wounded, and three Albanian civilians also wounded because they happened to be driving near the patrol.
