Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, were the killed and wounded policemen from this and other instance -- let's talk about this instance in particular, were these killed and wounded locals from Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. They came here for periods of three years to work there, and then they just stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to this and other incidents where the terrorists attacked or killed or wounded policemen or other individuals, how would the local Serb population react after these incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were scared, what else?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall an incident involving an OSCE vehicle and some Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. On that day, that vehicle hit an elderly woman, and the vehicle didn't want to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was there a local reaction or back-lash against the OSCE and those local persons working with the OSCE as a result of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they expected the OSCE to calm things down, but the OSCE was - how should I put this? - more and more on the side of the terrorists. They were helping them more than they were calming the situation down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is that how the rest of the local Serb population viewed the presence of the OSCE when they were in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What you just described, were those personal feelings or were they the sentiment of the local Serb civilians, as you viewed them or as you witnessed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were some individuals and -- I mean, well civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when the OSCE first came to Suva Reka, is it correct that they stayed at the hotel owned and operated by this Misko Miskovic or Nisevic, the Hotel Boss?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that apart from the OSCE presence, this Hotel Boss didn't have any other paying customers at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't anyone except for the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And these OSCE vehicles, during the time that they were residing at the Nisevic hotel, did they in fact also obtain their fuel for their vehicles from another business enterprise owned by this Nisevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nisevic didn't have a gasoline station. I don't know where they got their fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at some point in time the OSCE moved out of this hotel and moved into the Berisha family compound, and their entire operation moved with them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you know whether the Berisha family had a petrol station or a fuel depot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was only Jashar Berisha who worked at this gasoline station. It's only possible that they -- that he could have helped them in some way. I really don't know except for this Berisha who worked at the gasoline station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- now, after the OSCE mission left the Suva Reka area and when the NATO planes began their attack on Kosovo-Metohija and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, how did the local Serb community react to the NATO attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what kind of atmosphere or interaction existed between the local Serbs and the local Albanians during this time-period after NATO attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. After what attack?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: After the NATO -- after NATO started bombing the country.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Serbs stayed where they were, but Albanians started fleeing, like going away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, were there -- were there outages of the power, water, and other utilities during the period of the NATO bombardment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are we talking here about Suva Reka or are these general statements that could be anywhere in the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My question was meant to be related to Suva Reka. I see that I did not limit it to that, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The -- have you in fact established yet that NATO bombed anywhere near Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have not, and I don't know whether the outages are related to the NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: See, these general answers to these very general questions we do not find of any assistance to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, then I will move along to specific matters in the area of Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you hear about the bombing and destruction of the police building in Prizren around the 25th of March, 1999, by NATO aviation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that but I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you hear about casualties from this NATO attack, particularly the deaths of two policemen including one local reservist and one member of the PAP -- PJP stationed in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't know these people. I heard they got killed, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you know or have knowledge of a factory in Suva Reka itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on to that. Can you help us with the date? Around the 25th of March is imprecise, but can you be any more precise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really do not remember the date. I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was it -- do you know if it was before or after the Berisha killing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. With respect -- I had asked you also about whether you had any knowledge of a factory in Suva Reka itself that had been bombarded by the NATO aircraft?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in this factory. I don't know whether it was bombed, this factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, after the destruction of the Prizren police building, is it accurate that the communications within the police force were severely disrupted, including the computer database links between various police structures?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I don't believe the witness was in Prizren, so if the -- it's a question about the SUP and the functioning of the SUP in Prizren, I would object to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the -- we've already heard that the OUP in Suva Reka was answerable to the SUP in Prizren, and therefore communications between the two the witness may know about. So I think the evidence is within the -- the question is within the compass of his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If he knows, of course; he may not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, yes. There was a break-down in communications because of electricity for a while. It wasn't that it was -- well, say four or five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. And now during the period of March through May 1999, are you aware or do you have knowledge of local civilians, including both Serbs and non-Serbs, that were arrested by the Serbian police in Suva Reka for looting private homes in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand this. Could you repeat it once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. Do you know of local civilians from Suva Reka who were arrested for looting homes in Suva Reka, that is stealing from homes that -- and causing damage, during the time-period of March 1999 through May 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They were detained and arrested during the bombing, too. They were in prison during the bombing in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And these persons that were arrested in Suva Reka and imprisoned in Prizren, were -- did they include both ethnic Serbs and persons of other nationalities, including ethnic Albanians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part they were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, we could ask about one more incident that occurred during the month of March. Do you recall any incident at the Balkan Bet shop in the commercial area of Suva Reka on or about the 22nd of March, where a civilian, Bogdan Lazic, was killed or -- attacked and killed by terrorists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was this Lazic a local of Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was from the village of Sopina, that is to say 3 kilometres away from Suva Reka. That's where he lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did he have any -- strike that. Did he come from a -- from a large family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, it's -- I'll just move on. It's not that relevant. Now, if we could move to the date when you stated that the Berisha killings occurred, and if I could direct your attention first of all to the period in time when the lorries were being -- when the -- when the Cegar units were disembarking from their lorries. First of all, you stated that you had ran in that direction. How did the Cegar unit -- how did they travel in the direction that they were travelling? Were they in or on foot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were on foot, and they were spread out. That is to say that there was a distance of 5 to 6 metres between them, respectively, as they moved towards the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And on that day, did you have knowledge of any combat operations taking place towards or around the Restane area, between the terrorists and the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this happened every day, but I mean I -- well, as for Suva Reka and in the perimeter of, say, 2 or 3 kilometres I always moved about there, but I could not see everything that was going on in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At this time I would ask the usher to put up IC47, I believe it is, and I'll have a question or two relating to this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I could direct your attention to the screen in front of you. This is the exhibit -- one of the exhibits you marked earlier today, and I want to ask you about the house you were located at this position D. Am I correct that only you and your three colleagues were in the area of this house near D at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not three, four.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Four including yourself, that's what I meant. Now, am I also accurate --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I also accurate that the units you described as the Cegar units, that they were not -- they were not near this house. Is that correct? You were there alone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not in those two houses where we were. They were in these other houses by this house D and E, and to the left and to the right, that is to say they were ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you completed that answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that we were in houses D and E, and the Cegars were in the other houses around these houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would it be possible for you to indicate on this photograph the direction in which the Cegar unit was heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And perhaps -- is it possible to do a different colour so it can be distinguished from these markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could show us the general direction in which the Cegar unit proceeded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what can I do? I don't know. They started here, then here, and along this way and in this direction. This was their movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we have that saved as the next available number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC50, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I believe you stated in your direct examination that you were -- that you were all going along lost. You really didn't know where you were going or what you were doing. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it your impression that the other individuals with you were in the same state of mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know as for others, but when the assistant commander set out, he reached a particular house and then he ran away. He left us there by ourselves. So what can I add to that? If he ran away and he was the person to issue commands, he fled and I stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did he flee before Cukaric and Tanovic began shooting the four men behind the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He fled as soon as we arrived at that house when he heard firing from all directions; that's when he fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And so I can -- am I correct then that this was before Tanovic and Cukaric shot and killed the four individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- now, prior to this incident your patrol had not personally taken part in any actions or activities with this Cegar unit, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't take part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- and would it be accurate to state that you did not hear or have knowledge of any command or order given to your patrol to kill anyone on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, gentlemen, I can tell you what happened. We were in front of the building and we were observing what they were doing, but once Cegar 1 arrived he addressed the assistant commander and he just said: Get going. It wasn't our task and our job to do that with him. Had it not been for him, I don't think anything in the pizzeria would have happened or anything of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But this gentleman, this Cegar 1, at no point in time did he tell the -- you or the other individuals that were with you in front of the SUP, at no time did he tell you: Go out and kill people, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't. He didn't say anything. He only told the assistant commander: Get going with your men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to the men that were with you, the other fellows in your patrol, were they all locals from Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one person was from Suva Reka. The others were from elsewhere, say Uzice and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Had all of them been serving in the Suva Reka SUP for some time prior to this incident -- pardon me, I meant OUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- and another area I'd like to clear up from your examination testimony, you stated when at the pizzeria Jashari Berisha was brought. And I think you clarified that you do not have actual knowledge of whether he was at the OUP building or not. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw him being brought from that direction, from the SUP building. I could see the road they took; that's where I was standing. It's a proper road and you can see far ahead, and this was less than 200 metres away. He was brought there from that building. I'm pretty sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is the petrol station where Mr. Berisha worked also in that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now you indicated that you and your fellow colleagues that day drank some alcohol, two bottles to be precise. Was -- am I correct that all that alcohol was consumed prior to any shooting into the pizzeria or any grenades, rucne bombe, being thrown into the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have an approximate time that it took for the four of you to consume two bottles of alcohol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we drank it up like water so that we could relax.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the -- do you recall the volume of the bottles, that is to say whether these were 1 litre bottles of liquor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were 1 litre bottles, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just see. I might have a couple more questions. Allow me a moment to review my notes. Your Honours, I think I'm completed with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, just before you sit down, is there any help you can give us with the command structure within that police office? There was a measure of confusion yesterday about the positions held by certain people. Repanovic was said to be the head of the uniformed branch at Vitosevic was said to be the head of the criminal investigation branch. And it was vague who was in charge of the whole office. Can you assist on that and clarify on any of these?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can. I don't know whether I should be testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can. I don't know whether I should be testifying. I can ask the witness, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you can through the facility you have for leading questions, clarify what the witness told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will try to, Your Honour, and I hope my colleagues -- I hope I'm not using up too much of their time, but I will endeavour to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. K83, with respect to the OUP of Suva Reka, is it correct that the overall commander of this police station was Vitosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall what rank Vitosevic held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned Repanovic. Is it correct that Repanovic was merely a lieutenant within the structure of the OUP of Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And was Vitosevic's rank higher than Repanovic's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say, but he was -- he must have been of higher rank, him being the head of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now the other individual you named Nenad Jovanovic, am I correct that his post of -- I don't -- I think he was an assistant or -- rather than a deputy commander. Am I correct that that was the lowest police superior officer position within the structure of the Suva Reka OUP at the time, that is to say the lowest staresina [phoen] position within the OUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that clarifies the position, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I would just have one -- one or two more just to clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. On you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact in -- strike that. Am I correct that superior to Jovanovic in the hierarchy of the Suva Reka OUP, there was in addition to Repanovic another individual named Borisavljevic and that all these -- these two persons had positions superior to Jovanovic but inferior to Vitosevic, who was the chief of the OUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And the -- am I correct that the RDB that Mr. Nisevic was a part of, that was not formally a part of the OUP; they were a separate structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. His office was in the SUP building, but the DB offices were not within the same chain. They had nothing to do with the SUP itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I accurate then that Vitosevic, as the head of the OUP, had no command authority over the DB and the DB officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Vitosevic had no authority over the DB. He couldn't issue commands, he couldn't order the DB to do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, I think I clarified what Your Honours and I both wanted, so I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. K83, the name Jovanovic -- is it Jovanovic or Jevanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. And of the two persons Repanovic and Borisavljevic, which of them held the higher position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Repanovic did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Marcussen, can I ask you about the issue of action taken by Serb authorities in relation to the events affecting the Berisha family. Are you aware of the trial of Cukaric and Tanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. I was intending to put some questions in re-direct about this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why was that sort of evidence not led in direct examination, to give us the picture -- the complete picture that some action was being taken about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, primarily because this witness has only been a witness in that case and therefore cannot really speak to the -- to the details of that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So will we be getting other information about this so that we don't need to explore it at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The other reason why this witness hasn't been asked about it is it is our understanding that that second procedure -- the case before the -- that is now before the Belgrade Special Court only started years after and therefore is not the outcome of the investigation that the witness was involved in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We of course have extensive records and documentary evidence from those record, and they have been disclosed to the -- from the special court case and I'm sure the Defence has that as well. We have disclosed all of that material. If it would assist the Court, we can certainly make that available to the Court and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not necessary. You're the person who can judge whether it will be of assistance to us because we don't know anything about those proceedings. All I'm trying to do is establish the state of play. You're say saying that these are ongoing proceedings, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, I think these are matters for you to judge. I just wanted to be clear about the current situation, and I note that your explanation is that this is -- or these are proceedings which have arisen years after the events that we're considering. Now, Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will have a few. I can assist you in telling you that this Tanovic is dead and there are no proceedings against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. -- well, you have your first and last name and I cannot force myself to call you K and the number, so I will just address you with mister. I hope you won't mind.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: My name is Toma Fila and I appear on behalf of Nikola Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: First, to clarify, as regards to patrol comprising the four of you, to go back to that briefly, you mentioned there were four of you and there was no Tanovic, no mention of Tanovic at the time. And then you mentioned Cegar appearing and everything else. And then all of a sudden you see Cukaric and Tanovic taking out four Albanians. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When you set out on your patrol there were four of you. There was no Tanovic in the story yet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have omitted Tanovic, but he was a member of the patrol together with Nenad Jovanovic, the assistant commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And Cukaric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and Petkovic and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So that's five?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The four of us plus the assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, so we needed to clarify that. Then you were interrogated by an investigative judge in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So you were questioned by investigative judge in Belgrade. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: He put a few questions to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt my learned colleague. I had problems with this myself. I'm told that after we have posed a question we need to turn off our microphones because otherwise the voice will be picked up by the microphone and the voice distortion will not work. It's very inconvenient. I'm sorry, but that's apparently how we have to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: To repeat the question. You were questioned by Judge Dilparic, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: He had questions for you regarding the Berisha family and what those houses were like, and you said that as people they were always a bit on the dirty side. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, that they were hot-tempered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Then you were asked if Tanovic and Cukaric had any reason to hate these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did he ask you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And then you said: Well, I don't know. It is possible. There were OSCE monitors there, they were with them, they let them in their houses, they used their jeeps, they ran over a woman in Suva Reka and nothing happened. They were sort of -- well, no one could touch them for as long as the monitors were there. Is that -- this what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can we conclude therefore that the behaviour of Cukaric and Tanovic was sort of a revenge against the Berisha family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had any dispute or feud with the Berisha family.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But if we put this all in the context of the Berisha family treatment of the Serbs, could there have been a reason that this particular incident happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I conclude my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think at the end the witness was asked to speculate. He had already indicated he didn't know, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that's a pretty reasonable assessment of the situation. He had already said that he didn't know whether Tanovic and Cukaric had any dispute or feud with the Berisha family. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll be very brief and I will try to conclude before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. K83, my name is Mihajlo Bakrac, one of the counsel for General Lazarevic, and I will try to put a few questions to you so that we can conclude shortly. I would like to clarify something. You told my learned friend Mr. Ackerman that there was no army at the time in Suva Reka, and you confirmed that in your statement. My question, therefore, is the following: Is it correct that the army was on a mountain in the forest nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were outside of Suva Reka. They were never in the settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The place where the army was, is it called Dulje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me, since you were a reserve policeman, that the pass or the hill called Dulje is at the very entrance to the Crnjelovo gorge and it has certain strategic importance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know because of this strategic importance the Army of Yugoslavia was often attacked by the KLA at that very spot, at Dulje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To move on to another topic, you mentioned the Cegar police unit is it correct that the unit was stationed in the Balkan Hotel in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of, not all of them. Some were up at Dulje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you and your colleagues used a Russian make car called Gazik for your patrols and this was a bullet-proof vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may have a moment, Your Honours, I believe I will have no further questions. I have no further questions, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We -- I do have some questions. We have close to the break. I don't know whether Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There won't be any harm in overrunning for 15 minutes, if that's what you have in mind, and we'll start is a minutes later in the afternoon. It would be much more convenient than having to interrupt the witness somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, I think that's a good solution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: K83, you were asked whether on the -- on the -- on the 26th in the morning there had been a briefing where you had been given assignments. I just want to clarify that point. In the morning you had gone to -- you had gone with supplies and other things outside Suva Reka as I understand it. Had there been a briefing where that assignment had been given to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But during that briefing there had been no talk of any operation involving the OSCE house, the Restane road, or involving the assistance of the Cegar units. Is that how I should understand your answer to my learned friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I also think you said that Nenad Jovanovic looked surprised when Cegar 1 told him to get moving and join him in the operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was surprised because he didn't know why he should get going. He had regular work that he was supposed to do; that's why he was surprised and we were surprised, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But then -- so -- and that is why you say that you think that the whole thing started because Cegar 1 arrived. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, you have described how you were running towards the -- in the direction of the OSCE house and other houses. Would you describe all that movement as -- as a joint operation between people from the OUP and the Cegar units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could be put that way because -- well, we were sort of -- well, first they went and we went behind them and, well, sort of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So while you were told to take up a position in certain places, the Cegar units were taking care of other houses, so there was some sort of organised division of labour going on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You were also asked about the investigations that were carried out at the OSCE building and I have some questions about that. Now, first of all your evidence is that the person who bought -- brought Jashar Berisha down to the pizzeria, one of those persons was Todor Jovanovic. Is that the same Todor Jovanovic who participated on the investigation team that you provided security for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, crime scene technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So he knew what had happened at the pizza bar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he knew, since it got that far.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Would you -- I know you were at the pizzeria. But considering what happened at the pizzeria, hand-grenades being thrown, a lot of fire from automatic weapons, would that have been heard at the OUP, the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It wasn't that much -- I mean, it wasn't that strong a detonation, because there were buildings around and concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You explained that a number of people arrived, Vuksanovic, Djordjevic. Did other policemen come to the pizzeria during the day when you were sitting down at the position you might you remember you indicated with a B close to the kiosk by the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were a lot of people from the civil protection and from the municipality, from the TO -- well, I cannot refer to all those names now and remember all of them. Well, people came sort of out of curiosity to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was it an incident that people talked about in Suva Reka afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you speak to other of your colleagues about the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In your opinion, would your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That depends who the colleagues were, if I've understood your drift.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you remember who you spoke to about the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I don't know. They were colleagues, sort of everyday co-workers. I cannot remember exactly what their names were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were -- was this being spoken about to such an extent you think your superior officers would have heard about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I think that's a question that's within -- again, within the compass of the witness's experience and he can tell us if he has no idea.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: After the 26th -- well, let me put my question differently. You went down with the investigation team along the Restane road the day after the incident and you found a number of bodies. Were there any civilians that you came by in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: After the events in the first days after the -- the NATO bombings, did a lot of Albanians leave Suva Reka town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You were also asked about communication between the OUP and Prizren and you said that there had been a break-down in communication. I understand your evidence to be you're not entirely sure about when that break-down was. But while there was a break-down in communication, could you drive on the road between Suva Reka and Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could drive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was communication between the police station in Suva Reka and the SUP in Prizren by simply sending people back and forth between the two places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know whether the communication problems that occurred were overcome by sending people back and forth by road between -- for example, from the police station in Suva Reka and down to Prizren to make reports or receive instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your evidence was that the break-down in communication was caused by damage to electricity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was because of electricity. There was no electricity for four or five days, but the road between Prizren and Suva Reka was open.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What about communication either by telephone or by radio between Prizren and Suva Reka, was that impossible during this period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, certain types of radio communication did function. I don't know whether all the devices were operating, but one could communicate by radio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I want to ask you one separate question also. The immediate superior of yours Jovanovic, who was not at the pizzeria, was he aware of the events there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps afterwards, but I didn't see him on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'm thinking of afterwards. Did he become aware of these events after they had occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is this Jovanovic, is he charged, to your knowledge, before the Belgrade court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You were asked some questions about looting of houses and whether a number of people had been arrested between March and May. Do you know whether the houses that were looted were -- belonged to Serbs or to Albanians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And finally, you were asked about the communication -- no, sorry, you were asked about the point in time when you were drinking the two bottles of liquor. When you testified -- when I asked you some questions you said that you saw -- you saw Cukaric communicate on the radio. Was he communicating on the radio before, during, or after you had been drinking the alcohol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: While you were drinking the alcohol, did you discuss what would -- what you would do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Cukaric and Tanovic discussed throwing a hand-grenade in the pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well -- so that brings your evidence here to an end. Thank you very much for coming to the Tribunal to give this evidence. The court's going to rise now, and we will resume at 2.15. Just stay where you are until we've left the courtroom and then arrangements will be made also for you to leave. Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.47 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. There's a point regarding the evidence that we have been hearing from the two or three last witnesses, actually, that I thought I should just clarify. I realise that I omitted to clarify this earlier. We have heard evidence about the killing of Jashar Berisha. He is not among the scheduled victims on Schedule D. I just wanted to make that clear so there's no confusion later on about whether there's a mistake. His evidence is relevant to -- to the issue of how bodies from Suva Reka were moved around. And also, on the family-tree that was introduced through Shyrete Berisha, P2346, there are two children mentioned at the bottom of that family-tree, Genshi, and Graniqi Berisha, 4 and 2 years old. These two persons are not on the Schedule D either. I just wanted to make that clear to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's helpful. Are you taking the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: My colleague, Mr. Scully, will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who is the next witness, Mr. Scully?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Hysni Berisha. Mr. Berisha was originally a 92 bis (D) witness; his evidence has now been offered through 92 ter. The transcript in Milosevic can be found at P2281 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, just hold on, is that an alteration to the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The last witness running order running I have is the 22nd of September, which indicated Osman Kuci as the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. We had indicated via e-mail, I believe, to your Legal Officers and to Defence counsel yesterday that Mr. Kuci would not be called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: At all?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry. I didn't get that information. I spent some time on this, regrettably.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry that happened, Your Honour. We did notify the Legal Officers yesterday evening when we became -- when we came to that decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, good afternoon, Mr. Berisha.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please now make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be placed before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot hear the Albanian interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'll start again. Could you please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which is now before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Now, we have in front of us already a big bundle of paper which sets out the account you can give of various events. It includes the written transcript of the evidence you gave before when you came here, it includes statements you've given and other information. So there's a lot of information already before the court. The purpose of you being here today is so that counsel for the parties can ask you questions, either to add to that information, to explain it more fully, or to challenge it. The important thing for you to do is concentrate on the point that the questioner wants more information or any information about and try to confine the answer you give to the point that's being explored so that we don't go back over all the information we've already got. Time is short and precious in this building, and therefore it's important that we concentrate on the things that counsel want to ask you. The first person to ask questions will be for the Prosecution, Mr. Scully. Mr. Scully.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Would you like the relevant paragraph numbers or should I proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think in this case you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, can you please state your name and spell both your first and last name for the record.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: My name is Hysni, H-y-s-n-i, my father's name is Sylejman S-y-l-e-j-m-a-n, and the surname is Berisha, B-e-r-i-s-h-a.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Berisha, wrote do you live now?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: I live in Suhareke, Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And how long have you lived in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: From the day I was born on the 12th of April, 1948.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor dated 20 August, 2001, regarding the events in Suva Reka in 1998, 1999, and beyond?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Did you add information to that statement on 13 March 2002?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: For the record, that is Exhibit P2282.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, did you also testify in the Milosevic case regarding events in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: The transcript can be found at P2281.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, did you review those two statements with me last Friday, as well as yesterday, the 25th of October [sic]?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And even though you added some information to them, were the statements otherwise true and correct?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, very true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honours, my first question will relate to page 8 of Exhibit P2282, and may I have Exhibit P120 at page 2 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, did you visit the VJ firing range in Suva Reka in August 1999 with the British forensic team?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And it was the 1st of September, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: As soon as the photograph appears on your screen, can you tell me whether you recognise the location that is shown on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the firing range of the former Yugoslav army. It is between the villages of Korisha and Lubishte.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: How do you get to that location in terms of major roads you would take from the town of Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: If you leave from Suhareke, you go towards Prizren. About the 13th kilometre you can find this firing range.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: May I have Exhibit P123 at page 25 up on the screen next.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, when you visited that firing range, were you shown some items that had been recovered from the ground there?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. This was before visiting the site with the British forensic team, who worked at that site. On the 1st of September we assisted the opening of that grave site by this forensic team, and all these objects that you see on the monitor were found at this site, grave site.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Why were you shown the objects that have appeared on the monitor in P123?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: All these items with a code KRA were found at the mass grave at the firing range of the Yugoslav army, and these items were found when this grave site was opened. The code was KRA and they were shown to me to identify the missing people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to the numbers and letters that are written next to the objects, were those KRA codes next to the objects when you saw them for the purposes of identifying the items?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, are you saying these were found before the British forensic team did their work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. These here were found while the British team was working there, the British team opened the grave site. They were in the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, were you able to recognise a number of items that were shown to you and did you put your description of the items into your statement of 2001?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. These items that are shown on the monitor were identified by me and the family members of those people, and they were identified -- for example, KRA1036 is the handkerchief of Musli Berisha and his son and daughter identified it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibits P123, P133, and P134 are sequences of photos very similar to this one. I'm moving to admit them at this time based on this foundation and based upon the description in the statement. If the Court would like further foundation, I would need to show him each page, which I think would be rather time-consuming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there any objection to that course of action? Very well, you can proceed on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can I have P122 at page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to the left side of the screen, to the photo shown there, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph was found at the grave site, and I know the people who are in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Did you see that photograph recovered at the grave site?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. It was found on the 1st of September, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: May we have the next page, which is the photograph shown closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Who are the people who are depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: In the photograph you can see the wife of Hamdi Berisha, with her son Mirat, who were killed. Hamdi was killed and Mirat's four sisters were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: May I have Exhibit P125 at page 17. Your Honours, these -- the next four photographs were previously shown to Sherita Berisha and she had testified that the people depicted there were killed in the coffee shop but she was unable to provide the names of these witnesses. Because they are scheduled, I am simply going to ask this witness if he knows, based on his personal experience, who these people are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, taking a look at the photograph on your screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just seeing these photographs now they've got -- they've got names at the bottom of them. I don't think that's proper if he's going to identify the individuals if it has a name on it that can be read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I actually don't remember having a name from the other day if we -- we saw this photograph the other day and I don't think there was a name on it. I may be wrong, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: We're checking, but I think this is the only copy of the exhibit we have. These are family members and so I would submit that that goes to weight rather than admissibility of the identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on and let's see what we can do about it because -- can you check, though, whether this is the only copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: The -- we can also -- it's a little late on this one. For the next ones we can ask the court staff to zoom in on the photograph before it's displayed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the other exhibit is P2344, which has not only the name but that -- the persons were present in the coffee bar written on it. I don't know of an exhibit that doesn't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can lay some foundation about how he knows these people, I think some of the Court's concerns about the accuracy of the identification may be allayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm getting advice just now, Mr. Scully, that P2344 does not have the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: If that's the case, Your Honour, I would be delighted to use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's the recollection of the Bench, that we saw photographs without names. It may say "present in coffee bar," but without the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: If P2344 is a better exhibit, I'm delighted to use that one. I believed that it had the copies on it and the copy on our screen does have names written on them or at least family relationships written on it. Your Honour, may I suggest we eliminate this problem and future ones by just zooming in on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you're confident that the names will not show.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, proceed to use the one you've got on the screen, Mr. Scully, and when you use the best one do your best to avoid exposing the name before the witness has a chance to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, do you know the person shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, she's from my family. She's the fourth daughter of Hamdi Berisha and Selija Berisha and the youngest sister of Mirat. You saw Mirat in the former photograph, previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: When she was alive, how often did you see her?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Because we are close in our family, we met each other very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: May I have page 18, if you could just bring it up on the attorneys' screens before publishing it through the court usher to the witness. Alternatively, if court staff can publish it, I don't know need to preview it. That's perfect. Is that on the witness's screen? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, do you recognise the person shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Who is that person?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: She is Hanumshahe Berisha, the wife of Sait Musli Berisha, the wife of Hamdi Berisha, Avdi Berisha, Musli Berisha. From this family, 16 people were killed. She was the oldest one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: May I now have the photograph shown on page 24 with the same arrangement. And following 24, if it aids in preparation, I'll be asking for 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. She's the third daughter of Hamdi and Selija Berisha, or third sister of Mirat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And do you know her first name?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Arta or Zana Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: May I have page 28 with the same arrangement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Who is that person, Mr. Berisha?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: This is Musli Sahit Berisha, the eldest son of Hanumshahe Berisha and Hamdi's and Avdi's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: The next exhibit I'll ask for is P2351, drawing the Court's attention now to page 7 of Mr. Berisha's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, during the course of the investigations you've described in your statement, did you prepare a list of persons killed and missing in Suva Reka and provide it to the Prosecution in 2001?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I gave them a list that I had at the time. I have now an extended list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to the document that is on your screen, is that the extended list you just described?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: No, it doesn't start from number 1. This is just one page of that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: I think we ended up somewhere in the middle of that exhibit. It looks like that's page 7. I think it might actually be easiest to go to the last page.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the new list, with the additions that were made later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: What is different about that list from the list you provided in 2001?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: It is different because the former list did not have many of the names of the victims, and after the family members came and gave us names of missing people, then the list became this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Did you also remove some people from the original list?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. We just added to the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Did you remove any persons from the original list based on their membership in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: There are no KLA soldiers here in this list. This is a list of civilians. The list of soldiers is another one, so they are not included in this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Your Honours, speaking now generally about the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, in your statement, you used the terms "police" and "regular police." Can you please tell the Court who you include in that category.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: First I would like to point out that I never worked or been a member in the police or the VJ. I've only completed my military service. For me all the police forces that were present there during the war in Kosova included many forces such as local Serbs that I knew from the past and during the war saw in uniforms, be it police or military one and I differentiated them from regular police. I called them rather member of Territorial Defence; however, they were under the command of the regular police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, I apologise for interrupting, but can you just tell us how you define the terms "police" and "regular police." I'll ask you some of those other questions in a moment.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: In my opinion, a regular police was the public-order police; however, these formations also included civilian formations that were mobilised, either in the police or Serbian army. And this is what in broad terms I call regular police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: What type of uniform, if any, would the regular police wear?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: They had blue camouflage uniforms and solid blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Thank you. You also used the term "paramilitary." Can you please tell us what you mean by that term.

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: I had the opportunity to come across forces that were wearing other types of uniforms, such as black uniforms with different insignia. I thought they were paramilitaries and that they were operating in Suhareke region. And also I've seen uniforms of the regular police that I already described. The paramilitary uniform, for me to describe it, I always based on the fact that the special units wore black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Did you personally know some of the people you've described as paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, I knew many of these local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: And did you know that the people you knew and described as paramilitaries were not employed by the police on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Not before 1998. They were not employed by the police, but after this year they became members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Did you ever observe people you've described as paramilitaries and people you've described as regular police working together?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: When did you see them working together?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: During 1998 and 1999, especially after 24th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCULLY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we will proceed in the following order: General Lukic, General Pavkovic, General Ojdanic, General Lazarevic, Mr. Sainovic, and Mr. Milutinovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I represent Mr. Sreten Lukic in these proceedings, along with my colleagues Mr. Branko Lukic and Mr. Ozren Ogrizovic. And I have a couple of questions for you to try and clarify some points that you have testified to here today. I would ask you to pay close attention to what I ask you, and I would also ask you to make sure that your answers are the most concise and truthful answers possible, so that if you don't understand a question please ask me to repeat it. Now, first of all, sir, you've told us that you were never employed by the police. I want to ask you about your education. Did you have any education in any type of investigative activities?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know if it is necessary for me to answer this question, Your Honours, because I was asked the same question during my testimony in Milosevic trial. If you find it reasonable for me to answer it, I will, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think it is open to counsel to ask the same question as was asked in an earlier trial as a prelude to developing other questions that they wish to ask. So it would be helpful if you would answer that question again today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not trained in investigative activities. I am an attorney-at-law by profession. What made me investigate is the fact that 48 persons from my family were killed, from my extended family were killed. This is the reason why I got engaged into investigative activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, now did anyone assist you in your voluntary investigations that you conducted in June of 1999 and thereafter?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: No. I assisted others for the truth to come on to surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did your investigative work receive any support or assistance from the temporary government that was in place in Suva Reka or by any other body?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: On 13th of June, I began my investigative activities about the crimes that were committed. At that time there were no institutions in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, however, that at some point in time between June of 1999 and October 8th of 1999, there was a temporary government council established in the town of Suva Reka. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: What I said earlier refers to an earlier period. Later on, a commission was found for investigating war crimes that were committed in Suhareke municipality, and I was a member of this commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. And now isn't it also correct that the temporary government established in Suva Reka was established by Hashim Thaqi's political party, that is the political party of the KLA, and this existed until October 1999, when it was dismantled by UNMIK, the United Nations Mission in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: To me a temporary government is a civil administration that was -- in the beginning, as I said, Kosova was without administration. And this temporary government did not engage in investigations. We as family members of the victims became members of the commission for investigating war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just trying to see if my question had been answered. Isn't it correct that Hashim Thaqi's political party established a temporary government in Suva Reka that was dismantled in October of 1999 by UNMIK?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know exactly until what period this provisional government functioned. I don't know when it stopped functioning. Either it was at the time when the first election were held or in October, but when the UNMIK administration was established it took over all the civil powers in their hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, as part of your investigative work, were you composing any type of reports regarding the work that you were undertaking?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: As far as reports are concerned, I didn't compile any report myself. My work was exclusively a terrain work, a field work, in order to identify mass graves and persons that are missing to this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you have, I believe, identified here today this list that you've created. And correct me if I'm wrong, but this new extended list that was shown on e-court, it contains the names of persons who died in 1998 and is not limited to 1999, as you had originally stated in your statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: No. First of all, they did not die. All persons on that list did not die a natural death; they were killed by the Serbian police and military forces. The list includes names of victims that were killed during 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I believe your statement talks about the list being limited to 1999, but I'll move on. With respect to this list, you testified that there was -- well, first of all, does this list include civilians who were killed by the KLA in the Suva Reka municipality at any point in time during 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Nobody was killed in Suhareke by the KLA, be it a person from a Roma ethnicity or a Serb ethnicity or Albanian ethnicity -- at least I don't have any information of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were your investigations conducted to determine deaths of persons killed by the KLA or did you just focus upon ethnic Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Civilians killed, who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you investigate any Serb civilians who were killed during the relevant time-period and do they appear on your list?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: I would gladly conduct investigation about such cases, but they did not address me with any request of this kind, to investigate a Serb civilian that had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, you certainly knew about Serb civilians that had been killed by the KLA, did you not?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: As I said, I don't know of a case of a Serb killed by the KLA in Suhareke.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know the case of Bogdan Lazic killed in March 1999, at 1430 hours in the Balkan Bet shop that's referenced in your statement?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: I want to make a clarification here. On the 22nd of March, 1999, at around -- now I don't know exactly, but it was around 12.00, an incident occurred and to this day it is not clear who carried out that incident. It looks that it was a staged incident as a pretext to carry out the massacre that occurred the same day when ten Albanian civilians were killed, nine men and one woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you carry out investigations related to Mr. Lazic's killing?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I didn't because I didn't have any source of information. From what I learned from the diary of --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think you've answered my question --

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: Stanislav Niskovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction, Andrejevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think you've answered my question. I want to ask you about the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It would help us to have the complete answer to the question. The witness was explaining why he had no source of information I think. And then he goes on to say: From what I learned from the diary of. Now, could you complete that answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As I was saying in my previous answer, from the notebook of Stanislav Andjelkovic, who was a high official in Suhareke municipality, and the case of the killing of the Serb that was mentioned by the counsel and of these ten Albanians were not mentioned at all, it is just saying there that the local authorities are investigating an incident, an act of crime, and it's not clear whether this act of crime refers to the killing of this Serb or to the killing of the ten Albanian civilians. From the date when these Albanians were killed, the ten civilians, their bodies have not been found to this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The gentleman, Mr. Lazic, isn't it correct that he comes from the neighbourhood near the Bytyqi, Morina, Hoxha, and Kryeziu families?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. Mr. Lazic lived in Sopia village, which is 3 kilometres from Suhareke. Zoti Lazic has nothing to do with the Bytyqi brothers, Morina brothers, or Hoxha brothers in this particular case. He lived, Mr. Lazic lived, in Sopia village.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did he have other family members living in and around the Suva Reka municipality?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know that he worked in Suhareke municipality, and Sopia village is part of Suhareke municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we can return to the second list that you mentioned, the list that has KLA members who are deceased. First of all, did you give a copy of that list to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: HYSNI BERISHA
