utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's about the police paramilitary and VJ.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I can try and clarify that with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It would be helpful to us if that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, on page 4 of your statement you state that on 28th of March you saw different forces in the neighbourhood of Tavnik and you describe them as consisting of police, paramilitary, and VJ. Can you provide some more detail or any sort of description as to the forces that you saw there, the uniforms, the type of equipment they had, or weapons?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I told you, Madam, the uniform was different from the regular police. I don't recognise weapons, as I told you, but on top of their guns there were these big knives. And on both sides of their belt there were big knives, which was not a normal thing for normal policemen to carry. And they had painted faces, which shows that this was not the police of a normal state.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, you described -- you first say that you saw police. What do you mean in your statement when you say you saw police in the neighbourhood of Tavnik on 20 -- I'm referring to 28th March.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes, there were policemen as well, policemen in regular uniform, the normal one that we used to see before. So not all of them wore the same uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you have spoken about men in -- that had painted faces and that have knives, I understand, at the end of their weapons. Are these the men that you're referring to in your statement as paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The most terrifying people I have ever seen in my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Then you say that you also saw VJ. What do you mean when you say you saw VJ forces consisting of VJ on the 28th of March?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What do you mean by that when you say you saw the VJ?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I said it earlier. Not soldiers, not ordinary soldiers that we used to see before. On their heads you could only see their eyeballs, nothing else. And the same kind of gun that -- the knife at the end of it. I don't know what it's called -- as a matter of fact, I don't want to know what it's called.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And these people you just described are the ones you referred to in your statement as being VJ members or members of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: What do you mean by "VJ" -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You just answered yes. I'm not sure if you were responding to my question. I'm just trying to clarify for the Court. When you say you saw this men wearing masks and with the knife, are you -- is this what you -- the type of forces that you referred to as VJ in your statement?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Madam, the police uniform is blue. The military uniform is green. And then I explained earlier what they looked like.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And a final question. You saw all these different type of forces in the neighbourhood of Tavnik on 28th March; is that what you're stating?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes. This was the en masse expulsion of the inhabitants of Mitrovica, about 70.000 of them that were expelled forcibly from the town that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Hajrizi.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, these questions are about events on the 28th of March, and one of the things you say in your statement is: "In the street where we stayed, they started in one end to burn houses and told people to leave immediately." Now, who was it or which forces was it that did that, started to burn the houses and told people to leave immediately?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: The Serb army and the police, the Serbian police, and the paramilitary police --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, when --

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: -- forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you talk of the Serb army, can you tell us how they were dressed and equipped?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I said that they had green uniforms, military uniforms, in military colours, but it was not the usual one because they had these things on their heads that you could only see their eyes. And then at the end of the -- their guns, they had those knives, the bayonet, now I know what they're called, and that was not normal before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mrs. Hajrizi, that brings your evidence to an end. Thank you again for coming again to the Tribunal to give this evidence and for expanding it today. You're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: An application was made to revoke protective measures for a forthcoming witness, K75. There will be a written order issued granting that motion. We'll resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 27th day of September, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24
